videos.title: Private Snafu: Complete WWII Collection Vol. 1
videos.description: A complete collection of uncensored Private Snafu cartoons produced during World War II by Warner Bros. and the U.S. Army Signal Corps. These training cartoons used humor to teach soldiers important lessons.

videos.title: Superman: Billion Dollar Limited (1942)
videos.description: The Man of Steel must stop a gang of criminals from hijacking a gold train carrying a billion dollars. One of the classic Fleischer Superman theatrical short films.

videos.title: Popeye Meets Aladdin and His Wonderful Lamp (1939)
videos.description: Popeye and Bluto compete as genies to rescue Olive Oyl from an evil sultan in this feature-length Fleischer Brothers two-reel Popeye special.

videos.title: Fantasmagorie (1908)
videos.description: Created by Emile Cohl, this is considered one of the earliest examples of traditional hand-drawn animation. A stick figure encounters various morphing obstacles in a dream-like sequence.

videos.title: Humorous Phases of Funny Faces (1906)
videos.description: One of the earliest animated films ever made. J. Stuart Blackton draws comic faces on a blackboard that seem to come to life, predating the animation industry by years.

videos.title: Little Nemo (1911)
videos.description: Winsor McCay's groundbreaking animation based on his comic strip Little Nemo in Slumberland. One of the first examples of character animation, featuring remarkably fluid movement for its era.

videos.title: It's Got Me Again! (1932)
videos.description: A group of mice terrorize a cat through music and mayhem in this early Warner Bros. Merrie Melodies cartoon by Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising. One of the first cartoons nominated for an Academy Award.

videos.title: Let's Sing with Popeye (1934)
videos.description: Popeye leads a sing-along in this early Fleischer Studios cartoon, featuring the classic Popeye theme and bouncing ball format for audience participation.

videos.title: Sinkin' in the Bathtub (1930)
videos.description: The very first Looney Tunes cartoon, introducing Bosko and Honey. Bosko causes mayhem during his morning bath before picking up Honey for a drive in this musical short by Harman and Ising.

videos.title: Bosko the Talk-Ink Kid (1929)
videos.description: The very first Bosko cartoon, created as a test reel by Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising. A live-action animator interacts with the cartoon character Bosko in this historic milestone short.

videos.title: Felix the Cat: Doubles for Darwin (1923)
videos.description: Felix the Cat impersonates a missing link in a museum to help a professor, leading to a wild adventure with prehistoric creatures. A classic Pat Sullivan/Otto Messmer silent-era cartoon.

videos.title: Little Audrey: The Lost Dream (1949)
videos.description: Little Audrey falls asleep and enters a dream world where she battles fantastical creatures to rescue a baby dragon. A charming Paramount/Famous Studios cartoon.

videos.title: Little Ol' Bosko in Baghdad (1938)
videos.description: Bosko and Honey travel to the mystical city of Baghdad, where they encounter a fearsome genie and magic carpet in this colorful MGM cartoon by Harman and Ising.

videos.title: Old Mother Hubbard (1935)
videos.description: Ub Iwerks adapts the classic nursery rhyme in this colorful ComiColor cartoon. Old Mother Hubbard's dog gets into mischief while she searches for a bone at the market.

videos.title: Gabby: Fire Cheese (1941)
videos.description: The grumpy little town crier Gabby embarks on a comedic adventure involving a fire and some very precarious cheese-related situations in this Fleischer/Famous Studios short.

videos.title: Bosko and Bruno (1932)
videos.description: Bosko and his loyal dog Bruno go on a wild musical adventure in this early Merrie Melodies cartoon from Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising at Warner Bros.

videos.title: Wat's Pig (1996)
videos.description: Peter Lord's Oscar-nominated short film tells the story of two brothers — one raised by royalty, one by pigs — who switch lives in this witty and beautifully crafted Aardman clay animation.

videos.title: The Stolen Sun (1943)
videos.description: A classic Soviet animated film in which a bear steals the sun, plunging the world into darkness, and the animals must band together to rescue it. An early gem of Russian animation.

videos.title: Colonel Bleep Arrives on Earth (1957)
videos.description: The first color cartoon made for American television. Colonel Bleep, a space alien hero from the planet Futura, arrives on Earth and embarks on his first adventure with his deputies Squeak and Scratch.

videos.title: Panchito (1945)
videos.description: A Mel-O-Toons animated short following Panchito, a spirited rooster character, in a classic theatrical cartoon from the golden age of animation.

videos.title: The Case of the Kangaroo Kid (1963)
videos.description: A classic 1960s animated short featuring The Kangaroo Kid solving a mystery in this early television-era animation adventure.

videos.title: Paul Bunyan (1958)
videos.description: The legendary American tall tale comes to life as Paul Bunyan and his giant blue ox Babe perform extraordinary feats across the American frontier in this theatrical animated short.

videos.title: Aladdin (1958)
videos.description: The classic tale of Aladdin and his magic lamp is brought to life in this animated theatrical short, featuring the young hero battling a sorcerer for the princess's hand.

videos.title: Felix the Cat: Feline Follies (1919)
videos.description: The very first Felix the Cat cartoon. Felix navigates domestic misadventure in this landmark silent-era animation by Otto Messmer and Pat Sullivan that launched one of history's most iconic characters.

videos.title: The Tin Soldier
videos.description: Hans Christian Andersen's beloved fairy tale about a one-legged tin soldier who falls in love with a paper ballerina is adapted into a charming animated short.

videos.title: Fleischer Screen Song: Prisoner's Song (1930)
videos.description: A classic Fleischer Studios Screen Song cartoon featuring the famous bouncing-ball sing-along format, set to the popular 1924 song. Features richly detailed rotoscoped animation.

videos.title: Felix the Cat: Felix Minds the Kid (1922)
videos.description: Felix the Cat reluctantly babysits a mischievous infant who escapes into the neighborhood, leading to a chaotic chase in this early Pat Sullivan / Otto Messmer silent animation.

videos.title: Little Gray Neck (1950)
videos.description: A beloved Soviet animated film about a little duck injured and left behind when her family migrates south for winter, who must then survive predators on a frozen lake. A gem of Russian animation.

videos.title: Jack Frost (1934)
videos.description: The spirit of winter, Jack Frost, brings cold weather and icy magic to the world in this charming Ub Iwerks ComiColor cartoon from the golden age of theatrical animation.

videos.title: Hollywood Capers (1935)
videos.description: Buddy and his dog Cookie sneak onto a Hollywood movie set and cause comedic chaos as they stumble from one movie production to another in this early Warner Bros. Looney Tunes cartoon.
